Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Post-demo: hosting recommendation and concrete next steps

Hi Sam / Priya —

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap + concrete asks so we can align on the right hosting path (Hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private VPC):

Key signals from the demo
- 98th-percentile latency target: ~60 ms for single-token responses (svc-level SLA)
- Steady-state QPS: 220 requests/sec, average request = 48 tokens, with short tail spikes to ~520 rps for 3–5 minute windows
- Strict data isolation required for PII subsets, but primary need is predictable latency during peak shopping hours

Redwood recommendation (high level)
- Pilot on Hosted API with Dedicated capacity fallback configured by routing policy. Rationale:
  - Hosted gets you live fastest and covers most traffic patterns with our autoscaling; Dedicated pool reserved capacity will be the short path to meeting the 98th %-tile latency at 220 QPS and handling burst windows without throttling.
  - Private VPC/on-prem looks unnecessary at this stage given current compliance posture — we can re-evaluate if you need customer-managed networking or an on-prem package later.

Concrete asks / next steps
1) Please confirm expected request distribution by hour for a week (CSV is fine) — we need the per-minute burst profile to size dedicated pools.
2) Can you share which API endpoints must be within the strict PII isolation? (list of endpoints or examples)
3) I'll attach a short SOW draft for a 6-week pilot (Hosted + Dedicated reserved burst) — Ben will weigh in on pricing and commit tiers.

Attachments: Retailio_SLA_Questions.pdf (our SLA checklist we discussed) and Pilot_SOW-draft.docx (draft)

If you want we can lock a 30-minute planning call tomorrow to review pilot milestones. Proposed times: 10:00 AM PT or 1:00 PM PT.

Thanks —
Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Great, thanks Sam — attaching the CSV you referenced to our thread for record (Retailio_traffic_sample.csv).

Couple of clarifications based on your data and isolation ask:
- For the item-detail enrichment endpoint: we recommend tagging that route in our routing policy as "PII-sensitive" so requests are always routed to Dedicated capacity within the customer's region and also logged to the audit endpoint for KMS/HSM-backed keys. This satisfies both latency and audit requirements without moving you to Private VPC immediately.
- Sizing suggestion: baseline dedicated pool to cover 300 rps (buffer above steady-state) with autoscale burst headroom to 700 rps for short windows. We'll provide a cost estimate and the tradeoffs (larger reserved commit lowers unit price).

Next steps
- Ben, can you confirm what minimum monthly reserved commitment would be required to hit a price that keeps Retailio within their budget target?
- Sam / Priya, confirm the 10:00 AM PT call and we will send a calendar invite with an agenda: 1) pilot milestones & success metrics; 2) routing and PII audit plan; 3) pricing and commit options.
